verdict: TKO's revenue rose 21% to $1.36B as UFC jumped 60% on its new media-rights deal and a record UFC 329, lifting net income to $278M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, per Class A share; vs $0.47 a year ago

kpis.label: UFC revenue
kpis.note: +60% YoY on the new Skydance media deal and more events

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: operating cash flow of $472M minus capital spending

segments.name: UFC
segments.note: Mixed martial arts — media rights ($333M, boosted by the new Skydance deal that began in January 2026), live events, sponsorships and licensing. One extra numbered event and one extra Fight Night vs a year ago.

segments.name: WWE
segments.note: Professional wrestling — media rights ($256M), live events, sponsorships and consumer products. Roughly flat vs a year ago as lower live-event revenue offset media growth.

segments.name: IMG
segments.note: Sports marketing, media production and live-event hospitality (including On Location) — growth across the segment.

segments.name: Corporate & Other
segments.note: Everything outside the three leagues, including the Professional Bull Riders business.

segments.name: Eliminations
segments.note: Sales between TKO's own segments, removed so revenue is not double-counted.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative — running the leagues, selling sponsorships and media rights, and the back office; higher personnel and travel costs vs a year ago.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings, equipment and acquired rights over their useful lives — down from $129M a year ago.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $69.9M, partly offset by $9.6M of other income — a net $60.3M cost — plus $2.7M of equity losses from affiliates. Note: of the $277.9M net income, $179.2M belongs to noncontrolling interests (mainly Endeavor's stake in the operating company), leaving $98.7M attributable to TKO shareholders.
footerNote: TKO's partnership structure means most profit belongs to noncontrolling interests: reported net income was $277.9M, of which $98.7M was attributable to TKO Group Holdings shareholders. This page follows the reported net income line, as with other companies.

takeaways.title: UFC is carrying the growth
takeaways.text: UFC revenue rose 60% to $519M — media rights jumped on the new Skydance deal, and UFC 329 set records. UFC alone supplied almost all of TKO's $240M revenue increase.

takeaways.title: Margins expanded sharply
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA — the company's preferred profit measure, before interest, tax and non-cash charges — rose 54% to $556M, a 41% margin vs 32% a year ago.

takeaways.title: Shareholders keep a minority slice
takeaways.text: Of $278M of net income, $179M belongs to noncontrolling interests such as Endeavor; $99M was attributable to TKO shareholders ($1.33 per diluted Class A share). The company still raised full-year guidance and returned over $1.6B to equity holders this year.
